title: A constructible sheaf of modules on a qcqs scheme is a cokernel of a map between finite sums of extensions by zero of Lambda from affine etale objects
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $X_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, $\Lambda_X$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $\Lambda$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ let $j_{W!}\Lambda_W\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{X_{\Et}}(V,W)}\Lambda_X(V)$ (restriction along $\psi:V'\to V$ sending the summand of $\varphi$ to that of $\varphi\psi$ by the restriction of $\Lambda_X$; this is the presheaf $\mathcal O[h_W]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] for $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$, and its sheafification is the extension by zero $j_{W!}\Lambda_W$ of Stacks, Modules on Sites, 03DI). Let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then there are integers $n,m\ge0$, objects $U_1,\dots,U_n$ and $V_1,\dots,V_m$ of $X_{\Et}$ whose underlying schemes are affine, and morphisms $f:\bigoplus_{j=1}^mj_{V_j!}\Lambda_{V_j}\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nj_{U_i!}\Lambda_{U_i}$ and $g:\bigoplus_{i=1}^nj_{U_i!}\Lambda_{U_i}\to\mathcal F$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ such that the sequence
$$
\bigoplus_{j=1}^mj_{V_j!}\Lambda_{V_j}\xrightarrow{f}\bigoplus_{i=1}^nj_{U_i!}\Lambda_{U_i}\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F\to0
$$
is exact, i.e. $g$ is a cokernel of $f$. (Stacks states, for any Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, that the constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules are exactly the cokernels of this form with $U_i$, $V_j$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and that one can take them affine; only the direction 'constructible implies a cokernel of this form, with affine objects' is stated here, for finite $\Lambda$, the generality of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf].)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.73.6 (Tag 095N, label lemma-category-constructible-modules), the direction 'constructible implies cokernel'; its proof uses Modules on Sites, Lemma 093C (sites-modules-lemma-module-filtered-colimit-constructibles), Lemma 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian: constructible modules form an abelian subcategory) and the quasi-compactness of the constructible topology of the spectral space X (Properties, Lemma 094L and Topology, Lemma 0901).

proof.text: *Setting; finite sums of extensions by zero of $\Lambda$ from affine objects are constructible.* Write $\Mod=\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$; it is an abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] (kernels sectionwise, cokernels the sheafified sectionwise cokernels), so it has finite direct sums, and for an object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ write $P_W=j_{W!}\Lambda_W$ for the sheafification of $\Lambda_X[h_W]$ as in the statement. Let $U$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ whose scheme is affine. Then $U$ is quasi-compact (the spectrum of a ring is quasi-compact) and quasi-separated (the diagonal of an affine scheme is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact) [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $\Lambda$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module, so $P_U$ (which is $j_!\underline\Lambda_U$, the case $M=\Lambda$) is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible]. For finitely many affine objects $U_1,\dots,U_n$ the sum $\bigoplus_{i=1}^nP_{U_i}$ is constructible, by induction on $n$: for $n=0$ the sum is the zero sheaf, which is constructible by [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] (the stratification with the single stratum $X$, if $X\neq\emptyset$, or the empty one, the restriction being the constant sheaf with value the finite module $0$); for $n\ge1$ the split short exact sequence $0\to\bigoplus_{i<n}P_{U_i}\to\bigoplus_{i\le n}P_{U_i}\to P_{U_n}\to0$ of $\Mod$ has constructible outer terms, so the middle term is constructible since constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules are closed under extensions in $\Mod$ [thm-constructible-serre].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N ('In the proof of Lemma 03SA we have seen modules of this form are constructible'), which uses Lemma 03S8 (lemma-jshriek-constructible) and Lemma 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian)

proof.text: *A section gives a map from an extension by zero.* Let $\mathcal G\in\Mod$, $U$ an object of $X_{\Et}$ and $s\in\mathcal G(U)$. Regard $\mathcal G$ as a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules; by [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] (with $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$) there is a morphism of presheaves of modules $\beta:\Lambda_X[h_U]\to\mathcal G$ with $\beta_U(e_{\mathrm{id}_U})=s$, and by the universal property of the sheafification $\theta:\Lambda_X[h_U]\to P_U$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] there is a unique morphism $\sigma_s:P_U\to\mathcal G$ in $\Mod$ with $\sigma_s\circ\theta=\beta$. Put $e_U=\theta_U(e_{\mathrm{id}_U})\in P_U(U)$; then $(\sigma_s)_U(e_U)=s$. Consequently, for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ and every pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar x$, the induced map on stalks $(\sigma_s)_{\bar x}:(P_U)_{\bar x}\to\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] (the map of colimits induced by the components of $\sigma_s$) sends the germ of $e_U$ at $(U,\bar u)$ to the germ of $s$ at $(U,\bar u)$.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 093B (sites-modules-lemma-module-quotient-direct-sum) and the equation after Lemma 03DI (Hom(j_{U!}O_U, F) = F(U)), which give the surjection Psi of the proof of Etale Cohomology Lemma 095N (via 093C)

proof.text: *Stalkwise surjectivity at one geometric point from finitely many affine objects.* Let $\mathcal G\in\Mod$ be constructible and $\bar x$ a geometric point of $X$. The stalk $\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ is a finite set [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-stalks]; write $\mathcal G_{\bar x}=\{t_1,\dots,t_r\}$. The pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar x$ form a cofiltered category [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so the stalk is a filtered colimit and each $t_k$ is the germ of a section $s_k'\in\mathcal G(V_k)$ at some pointed etale neighbourhood $(V_k,\bar v_k)$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] (with $W=V_k$) there is an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(U_k,\bar u_k)$ with a morphism $(U_k,\bar u_k)\to(V_k,\bar v_k)$; the restriction $s_k=s_k'|_{U_k}$ has the same germ $t_k$ (compatibility of the colimit coprojections with the transition maps). By step 2 we get $\sigma_k=\sigma_{s_k}:P_{U_k}\to\mathcal G$ whose stalk map at $\bar x$ hits $t_k$. Let $g=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_r):\bigoplus_{k=1}^rP_{U_k}\to\mathcal G$ be the induced morphism, so $g\circ\mathrm{in}_k=\sigma_k$ for the coprojections; by functoriality of stalks $(\sigma_k)_{\bar x}=g_{\bar x}\circ(\mathrm{in}_k)_{\bar x}$, so every $t_k$ lies in the image of $g_{\bar x}$, i.e. $g_{\bar x}$ is surjective. (If $\mathcal G_{\bar x}=0$ one may take $r=0$.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N: 'Since every stalk F_x is a finite type Lambda-module and since Psi is surjective, for every x in X there is an I' such that x is not in T_{I'}' (here the finitely many summands of Psi = sum over pairs (U,s) with U affine are chosen directly)

proof.text: *The sets $T_\sigma$.* Let $\mathcal G\in\Mod$ be constructible. For a finite family $\sigma=(U_k,\sigma_k)_{k\in K}$ of affine objects $U_k$ of $X_{\Et}$ and morphisms $\sigma_k:P_{U_k}\to\mathcal G$ let $g_\sigma:\bigoplus_{k\in K}P_{U_k}\to\mathcal G$ be the induced morphism, $C_\sigma=\operatorname{Coker}(g_\sigma)$ in $\Mod$ and $T_\sigma=\operatorname{Supp}(C_\sigma)=\{y\in X: (C_\sigma)_{\bar y}\neq0$ for some geometric point $\bar y$ over $y\}$. (a) $C_\sigma$ is constructible, as the cokernel of a morphism between constructible sheaves (step 1 and the hypothesis on $\mathcal G$) [thm-constructible-serre]; hence $T_\sigma$ is a constructible subset of $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible]. (b) The underlying abelian sheaf of $C_\sigma$ is the cokernel of the underlying morphism of abelian sheaves: in $\Mod$ the cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], whose underlying abelian sheaf is the sheafification as a presheaf of abelian groups [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], which is the cokernel in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; and the stalk functor at a geometric point $\bar y$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $(C_\sigma)_{\bar y}=\operatorname{Coker}((g_\sigma)_{\bar y})$; thus $(C_\sigma)_{\bar y}=0$ iff $(g_\sigma)_{\bar y}$ is surjective. (c) If $\sigma\subseteq\sigma'$ (a subfamily), then $g_\sigma=g_{\sigma'}\circ\iota$ with $\iota$ the inclusion of the partial sum, so the image of $(g_\sigma)_{\bar y}$ is contained in that of $(g_{\sigma'})_{\bar y}$ (functoriality of stalks); by (b), $(C_\sigma)_{\bar y}=0$ implies $(C_{\sigma'})_{\bar y}=0$, hence $T_{\sigma'}\subseteq T_\sigma$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N: 'T_{I'} = Supp(Coker(...)). By the very definition of constructible sheaves, the set T_{I'} is a constructible subset of X' (this is Lemma 09YS (3), lemma-support-constructible, with Lemma 03RZ for the cokernel)

proof.text: *Every point is avoided by some finite family.* Let $\mathcal G$ be constructible and $x\in X$; choose a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ lying over $x$ (e.g. $\operatorname{Spec}$ of an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$) [def-weil-geometric-point]. By step 3 there is a finite family $\sigma^x$ as in step 4 with $(g_{\sigma^x})_{\bar x}$ surjective, so $(C_{\sigma^x})_{\bar x}=0$ by step 4 (b). By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible] (i), applied to the constructible sheaf $C_{\sigma^x}$ (step 4 (a)), the stalk of $C_{\sigma^x}$ then vanishes at every geometric point lying over $x$, i.e. $x\notin T_{\sigma^x}$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N ('for every x in X there is an I' such that x is not in T_{I'}'), with the independence of the support from the geometric point (paragraph before Definition 04FS, Remark 04FN)

proof.text: *Quasi-compactness of the constructible topology.* With the families $\sigma^x$ of step 5, $(T_{\sigma^x})_{x\in X}$ is a family of constructible subsets of $X$ (step 4 (a)) with $\bigcap_{x\in X}T_{\sigma^x}=\emptyset$ (step 5: $x\notin T_{\sigma^x}$). The underlying space of $X$ is spectral, $X$ being quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], so there are finitely many points $x_1,\dots,x_p$ with $\bigcap_{l=1}^pT_{\sigma^{x_l}}=\emptyset$ [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-finite-intersection]. Let $\sigma$ be the concatenation of the finite families $\sigma^{x_1},\dots,\sigma^{x_p}$ (a finite family of affine objects $U_1,\dots,U_n$ with morphisms $P_{U_i}\to\mathcal G$). Each $\sigma^{x_l}$ is a subfamily of $\sigma$, so $T_\sigma\subseteq T_{\sigma^{x_l}}$ for all $l$ by step 4 (c), hence $T_\sigma\subseteq\bigcap_lT_{\sigma^{x_l}}=\emptyset$ (if $p=0$, then $X=\emptyset$, $\sigma$ is empty and $T_\sigma\subseteq X=\emptyset$).

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N: 'we have emptyset = intersection of the T_{I'}. Since X is a spectral space by Properties, Lemma 094L the constructible topology on X is quasi-compact by Topology, Lemma 0901. Thus T_{I'} = emptyset for some I' finite'

proof.text: *A finite surjection onto every constructible sheaf.* With $\sigma$ of step 6, every geometric stalk of $C_\sigma$ is $0$ ($T_\sigma=\emptyset$). The morphism $0\to C_\sigma$ of underlying abelian sheaves is therefore an isomorphism at every geometric stalk, hence an isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; so the identity of $C_\sigma$ and the zero endomorphism agree after forgetting the module structure, and since a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules is a morphism of the underlying abelian sheaves with a linearity property [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] (two morphisms with the same underlying morphism are equal), $C_\sigma=0$ in $\Mod$. In the abelian category $\Mod$ a morphism with zero cokernel is an epimorphism. Conclusion: for every constructible $\mathcal G\in\Mod$ there are $n\ge0$, affine objects $U_1,\dots,U_n$ of $X_{\Et}$ and an epimorphism $\bigoplus_{i=1}^nP_{U_i}\to\mathcal G$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N: 'it suffices to prove that given a constructible module F there is a surjection (+)_{i=1..n} j_{U_i!}Lambda_{U_i} -> F for some affine objects U_i'

proof.text: *The presentation.* Apply step 7 to $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$: there are affine objects $U_1,\dots,U_n$ and an epimorphism $g:\bigoplus_{i=1}^nP_{U_i}\to\mathcal F$. Let $\kappa:\mathcal K\to\bigoplus_iP_{U_i}$ be the kernel of $g$ in $\Mod$; $\mathcal K$ is constructible, as the kernel of a morphism between constructible sheaves (step 1 and the hypothesis) [thm-constructible-serre]. Apply step 7 to $\mathcal G=\mathcal K$: there are affine objects $V_1,\dots,V_m$ and an epimorphism $h:\bigoplus_{j=1}^mP_{V_j}\to\mathcal K$. Put $f=\kappa\circ h$. In the abelian category $\Mod$: $g\circ f=0$; the image of $f$ equals the image of $\kappa$, which is $\operatorname{Ker}(g)$, because $h$ is an epimorphism; and $g$ is an epimorphism. Hence $\bigoplus_jP_{V_j}\xrightarrow{f}\bigoplus_iP_{U_i}\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F\to0$ is exact, i.e. $g$ is a cokernel of $f$ (an epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel, and $\operatorname{Coker}(\kappa\circ h)=\operatorname{Coker}(\kappa)$ as $h$ is an epimorphism).

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N: 'Since the category of constructible modules is abelian (Lemma 03RZ) it suffices to prove ... a surjection', written out

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 095N and kept (direction constructible => cokernel, affine U_i, V_j, Lambda finite). Proof written in eight steps along the proof of 095N: finite sums of j_{U!}Lambda_U with U affine are constructible (03S8 via lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible, extensions by 03RZ = thm-constructible-serre); a section s in G(U) gives P_U -> G hitting s (free Yoneda + sheafification); at each geometric point finitely many affine summands are stalkwise surjective (finite stalks, new node; germs over affine neighbourhoods); T_sigma = Supp(Coker) is constructible (new node, Stacks 09YS (3)) and decreasing in sigma; every x avoided by some sigma^x (independence of the geometric point: clause (i) of the support node, Stacks 04FS 'any (some)'); finitely many suffice by quasi-compactness of the constructible topology (094L via lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral and new node for 0901); zero cokernel by conservativity of stalks; the presentation from the epi onto F and onto its constructible kernel (written out; Stacks only says 'the category is abelian'). Deviation in form only: Stacks starts from the infinite surjection Psi of Modules on Sites 093C over all pairs (U,s); here the finitely many pairs needed at each point are taken directly, which is the only use the proof makes of Psi, and avoids stalks of infinite sums. stmt_deps unchanged. Three new nodes: lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-stalks, lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible, lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-finite-intersection (all unsplit; the last is a few lines from Mathlib compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology, not one).

reviewed.note: Split reviewed: 8 steps along Etale Cohomology 095N (finite sums of j_{U!}Lambda constructible; sections give maps from j_{U!}Lambda; stalkwise surjectivity from finitely many affine neighbourhoods using finite stalks; the constructible supports T_sigma of the cokernels; a point is avoided by some family; quasi-compactness of the constructible topology gives a finite family with empty support; conservativity of geometric stalks; the presentation via the kernel). Correct; the finite families replace Stacks' infinite surjection Psi. Three new unsplit nodes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_free_etale_presentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (hF : IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf F) : let P : X.Etale → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) := fun W => (presheafToSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj W ⋙ ModuleCat.free Λ) ∃ (n m : ℕ) (U : Fin n → X.Etale) (V : Fin m → X.Etale), (∀ i : Fin n, IsAffine (U i).left) ∧ (∀ j : Fin m, IsAffine (V j).left) ∧ ∃ (f : (∐ fun j : Fin m => P (V j)) ⟶ (∐ fun i : Fin n => P (U i))) (g : (∐ fun i : Fin n => P (U i)) ⟶ F) (w : f ≫ g = 0), Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ g w))
lean.note: Uses the ModuleCat-valued encoding of modules over the constant ring sheaf authorized by def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves; the sheafified free constant-coefficient Yoneda presheaf is the extension by zero in this encoding. No compactification or separatedness hypothesis is imposed on the affine etale objects.

reviewed_lean.note: qcqs X as CompactSpace/QuasiSeparatedSpace; finite comm Λ (zero ring allowed); F in recorded ModuleCat encoding with IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf; j_{W!}Λ_W = sheafified uliftYoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free (no landed ModuleCat-encoding j_! exists; SheafOfModules ExtensionByZeroPresheaf/QuotientJShriek are the ring-sheaf encoding); Fin n/Fin m families with IsAffine .left; ∐ finite sums; g cokernel of f via IsColimit CokernelCofork; full names #checked
